response.title: can i charge a power station from my car during a power outage
response.answer:
Yes! You can charge a portable power station from your car during a power outage. In fact, it's a useful way to keep your power station running during a multi-day outage, especially if you don't have solar panels or a generator.

There are three main ways to do it.

1. Through your car's 12V outlet (easiest)
Shop

Most portable power stations from brands like EcoFlow, Jackery, Anker, and Bluetti support charging through a vehicle's 12V accessory outlet.

Charging power: Typically 60–120W.

Charging time: A 1,000Wh power station might take 10–20 hours.

Equipment: Usually a 12V car charging cable.

Best for: Emergency charging without modifying your vehicle.

Keep the car engine running while charging to avoid draining the starter battery.

2. Through a DC-to-DC charger (much faster)
Shop

Some power stations support dedicated alternator charging systems.

Charging power: Approximately 300–800W, depending on equipment and vehicle.

Charging time: A 1,000Wh power station could charge in roughly 1.5–4 hours.

Equipment: Compatible alternator charger and proper wiring.

Best for: Extended power outages when you need to recharge frequently.

This is generally the most effective option if your vehicle and power station are compatible.

3. Through a car inverter

A DC-to-AC inverter converts your car's 12V power into household AC power, which can then charge your power station.

Charging power: Depends on inverter capacity and wiring.

Advantage: Works with many power stations that have AC charging.

Disadvantage: Less efficient because power is converted twice.

A high-power inverter generally needs a properly fused, direct battery connection rather than a standard 12V accessory outlet.

How much fuel would you use?

For a typical gasoline vehicle idling to recharge a power station:

Charging method

	

Approx. charging power

	

Time for 1kWh delivered




12V outlet

	

100W

	

10–13 hours




DC-to-DC charger

	

500W

	

2–2.5 hours




Fast alternator charger

	

800W

	

1.3–1.7 hours

These are estimates; charging losses, tapering, vehicle electrical capacity, and battery conditions affect results. Fuel consumption varies substantially by vehicle, and idling is often less fuel-efficient than using a dedicated generator.

Important safety precautions: Never idle a gasoline or diesel vehicle in a garage, even with the door open. Keep it completely outdoors and away from windows, doors, and air intakes. Also check your vehicle's alternator capacity and the charger's compatibility before installing a high-power system.

Two questions

What car do you have? (For example, Toyota RAV4, Ford F-150, Tesla Model Y.)

What power station do you have or plan to buy? (For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, Jackery Explorer 1000.)

With those two details, I can tell you how quickly you can charge it, which charging method will work, and whether you can realistically use your car as a backup power source during a multi-day outage.
